notes: e1 (lt3-e1) is still verbatim in the unchanged snapshot src-apple-legal-location.txt. Beat 2 now reads 'On iPhone, with Significant Locations and Routes on, it keeps track of where you've recently been, how often, when, and your routes.' Dropping 'Apple says' is within e1. e1 is Apple's direct statement of what its own software does ('Your iPhone ... will keep track of places you have recently been, how often and when you visited them, and the routes you take'). The single-origin justification (platform owner documents its own feature) covers stating it plainly. Both qualifiers are kept (setting on; recently). The beat 6 use ('If it's on, it's on your phone right now') is supported. The new visual direction is labelled Illustration, uses generic place names and is not styled as iPhone Settings. Acceptable. This pass covers wording against evidence only. The packet-level provenance fix in round-5-notes.md (lastCheckedAt refreshed without a recheck) must still be made.

e2 (lt3-e2) is still verbatim. Beat 4 'Apple says it can't read it.' is attributed and no stronger than e2. Recommended, not blocking: the line now directly follows the Android beat, whose last subject is Google's Timeline. 'It can't read it' therefore leans entirely on the word 'Apple' to show it means the iPhone record. Restoring two words removes the ambiguity: 'On iPhone, Apple says it can't read it.' The caption limit on untested encryption is unchanged and correct.

e3 (lt3-e3) is still verbatim, and the caption path matches it exactly. That is not why this fails. It fails because this claim is how the episode resolves its promise ('Is my phone keeping a record of where I go, and how do I check?'), and the cut removed it from the video before the twist. (1) CLAUDE.md requires the promise to be resolved before the twist. The 'how do I check' half now appears only in the caption, plus an on-screen pointer ('Where to find it: see the caption') inside the twist itself. (2) The script has no 'takeaway' beat, so evaluateCreativeRules (packages/content/src/creative.ts, lines ~69-80) raises 'missing_takeaway' and 'twist_before_takeaway'. Both are gate blockers, so the episode cannot reach verified whatever the review verdicts. (3) 'Go check.' is an instruction whose essential how-to is not in the video; captions are truncated on Reels. Required fix, which respects the owner's note (no how-to-remove or delete steps): insert a short takeaway beat between beat 4 and the twist. Role 'takeaway'. Narration: 'Here's where each one lives.' On-screen: 'iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Significant Locations & Routes' and 'Android: Google Maps > profile picture or initial > Your Timeline'. claimIds: c-iphone-setting-path, c-android-timeline-path. That is about 3-4 s. Do not use 'look' for iPhone: viewing on iPhone is not documented in these sources. The twist's 'Where to find it: see the caption' card can then go. Also update this claim's locations to match where it is actually used.

e4/e5 (lt3-e4, lt3-e5) are still verbatim. Beat 3 is unchanged. Beat 4 'Google keeps it on your phone, unless you back it up.' is supported. e5 says Google saves 'each of your devices' precise locations to that device'. e11/e16 make backup an opt-in encrypted copy on Google's servers, and the line now carries that exception. Dropping 'Google says' is acceptable on the same platform-owner basis as beat 2. Optional, recommended but not blocking: widen the caption limit to 'Apple and Google describe their own storage and encryption; this video does not test it.' so the unattributed storage statement is still marked as the vendor's own account. This pass covers wording against evidence only. The packet-level provenance fix in round-5-notes.md must still be made.

e6 and e15 (lt3-e6, lt3-e15) are still verbatim, and the caption path 'Google Maps > profile picture or initial > Your Timeline' matches. This fails for the same structural reason as c-iphone-setting-path. The 'how do I check' answer was moved out of the video into the caption, with only a pointer inside the twist. That leaves the promise unresolved before the twist and trips the 'missing_takeaway' and 'twist_before_takeaway' gate blockers. Required fix: put the path back on screen in a short takeaway beat before the twist (see the c-iphone-setting-path record for exact wording), without the turn-off or delete steps the owner removed. Update this claim's locations to match where it is actually used.
e10 (lt3-e10) is still verbatim. Beat 3 'Google Maps Timeline is off until you turn it on', the on-screen '(off by default)' and the caption are unchanged and supported.

e11 and e16 (lt3-e11, lt3-e16) are still verbatim. Beat 4 'unless you back it up' presents backup as the viewer's action, consistent with e16 (separate opt-in per device). The caption 'optional backups are encrypted copies on Google's servers' is supported.

e12 and e17 (lt3-e12, lt3-e17) are still verbatim. Twist 'Or never: then it's kept until you delete it.' matches e12 ('You'll keep your Timeline based on your auto-delete settings, or until you delete it') together with e17 (the Don't auto-delete activity option). Dropping 'Google says' is fine. It is Google's own documented retention rule for its own feature, and the sentence is scoped to Google Maps by the preceding clause. The on-screen 'Off = kept until you delete it' is unchanged.

e7 (lt3-e7) is still verbatim. The claim is now used only in the caption Limits ('turning Timeline off isn't the same as deleting it (Turn off and delete activity)'), which it supports. Removing the in-video turn-off and delete steps does not withhold an essential instruction. The video no longer tells anyone to turn it off, so no viewer is left thinking that turning it off erases the data, and the caption keeps the distinction. Required (ledger housekeeping): the claim's locations still say ['narration', 'visual', 'caption']. Set them to ['caption'] so the ledger matches the script.

e13 (lt3-e13) is still verbatim. After the cut, no narration, on-screen line or caption sentence asserts that Timeline shows where and how you traveled. The claim is listed in script.claimIds but backs nothing, while its locations say ['narration']. That breaks no publishing rule, but the ledger no longer describes the script. Required: either drop it from script.claimIds and set locations to [] (or remove it from the version), or, if the restored takeaway beat implies the Android path is where you view the Timeline, add it to that beat's claimIds and set locations accordingly.

e14 (lt3-e14) is still verbatim. It is used only in the caption Limits, unchanged. It also matters more now: beat 4 says plainly 'Google keeps it on your phone', and this caption caveat that other Google settings can hold location info stays essential. Keep it.

e8/e9 (lt3-e8, lt3-e9) are still verbatim, and 3/18/36 months match exactly. Twist 'You can set Google Maps to auto-delete it after three, eighteen or thirty-six months.' is unchanged and supported. The on-screen 'Timeline auto-delete: 3, 18 or 36 months, or off' is unchanged.
